transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Gomez (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Paperlane Head of ML), Arjun Singh (Paperlane CTO), Priya Nair (Paperlane Platform)

Summary:
Paperlane is evaluating Redwood for a low-latency customer-facing summarization service. Primary interests: time-to-first-token (TTFT) for PLG onboarding, free/trial credits to run a quick prototype, and tradeoffs between Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Security posture (SOC 2, SSO, KMS) and latency/cost buckets are key decision factors.

Topics discussed:
- Quickstart/PLG flow and estimated TTFT
- Free credits allocation and what they cover
- Hosting options: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, data retention
- Performance: latency percentiles, batching, KV cache, quantization
- Next steps and ownership

Transcript (note: transcription imperfect; occasional mislabels):
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everybody thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro, I'm Alicia, AE on this account, Daniel from our SE team will cover technical fit.
[00:07] Maya: Hi Alicia, hi Daniel, Maya here. we're excited - we built a prototype and want to understand how fast we can get to first token for customers.
[00:12] Arjun: Arjun, CTO. mostly focused on hosting options and security.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, platform - I'll be running any pilot infra for us.
[00:20] Daniel: Great. high level: Redwood offers a hosted API that is PLG-friendly with free credits to run a quickstart prototype, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private options (VPC or on-prem) for regulated workloads.
[00:31] Maya: can you quantify TTFT? like, from signup to first successful API call for a dev?
[00:36] Alicia: yeah good question. typical PLG path is account creation, SDK install, use our quickstart curl or example repo — most teams hit first token in under an hour; with pre-provisioned credits and our sample prompts it can be <20 minutes. for larger orgs we do onboarding templates.
[00:55] Maya: hmm okay — is that time including model warmup or cold KV cache hits?
[00:59] Daniel: that's a mix. quickstart uses smaller model variants we verify for latency; warmup isn't usually required for a single dev call. for production traffic you see better p99s after KV-cache warmed and with batching on. our runtime supports prefix caching and persistent KV across requests in Dedicated.
[01:20] Arjun: what's the difference in p50/p95 between Hosted and Dedicated? ballpark numbers?
[01:24] Daniel: ballpark — Hosted low-touch models: p50 ~ 60-90ms token latency for compact decoders in our EU/US regions, p95 often <350ms depending on seq length. Dedicated with pinned GPU and optimized kernel selection gets p50 ~ 30-50ms and p95 ~100-180ms for similar payloads, again varies with sequence length. private on-prem will depend on your HW.
[01:48] Maya: those are optimistic, especially for long-form summarization. our seq lengths go up to 2k tokens sometimes.
[01:54] Daniel: right, for 2k you'll see higher el latency; for longer sequences we recommend batching and offloading KV or using model variants tuned for long context. quantized variants reduce cost but add a small latency tradeoff.
[02:08] Priya: on Private/VPC — what does Redwood require from our side? firewall rules, outbound connectivity?
[02:13] Alicia: for Redwood Private (VPC) we run a control plane handshake but data plane can stay in your VPC. typical setup: allow secure egress to specific management endpoints, we support SAML SSO, you manage KMS/HSM integration for keys. if fully on-prem we provide a package but it requires more ops work.
[02:31] Arjun: we must check with security — SOC 2 is mandatory, also audit logs retention and key control.
[02:37] Alicia: we can share SOC 2 attestation and our security whitepaper. Audit logs are available in Redwood Console with token-level breakdowns and export options.
[02:47] Maya: credits — how many free credits do you typically give for a quickstart? and what's covered?
[02:52] Alicia: standard trial covers $5k equivalent in compute for 30 days for qualified signups; covers generation, embeddings... excludes heavy sustained Dedicated reserved usage. credits are meant to run realistic prototypes and benchmarks.
[03:05] Priya: does the trial include throughput/load testing? we're worried about being rate-limited during a demo to stakeholders.
[03:11] Daniel: we can temporarily increase rate limits for pilot customers; we'll work with you to set expected QPS. for long-duration load tests we recommend a small Dedicated burst window or run tests against a local quantized runtime to validate.
[03:26] Arjun: ok — cost math. how do you recommend we estimate token cost for a 1M token/day workload?
[03:33] Daniel: depends on model & batching. with batching and prefix caching you can drastically reduce token counts. rough example: hosted medium model with 1M tokens/day might be $X/day in hosted pricing; Dedicated becomes attractive above certain sustained QPS because of reserved capacity discounts and predictable throughput. we can send a simple calc sheet.
[03:52] Maya: objection — we already have some infra and are considering self-host. what's Redwood's argument vs building our own inference stack?
[03:59] Alicia: fair. building gives control but costs time (ops, optimizations, kernel tuning). Redwood provides a production runtime, smart routing, autoscaling, and observability; you avoid the upfront 3-6 month infra effort and ongoing maintenance. also rollouts and fallback policies are built-in.
[04:17] Maya: do you have references in our vertical? (customer-facing summarization for news)
[04:21] Alicia: yes, we'll share a couple anonymized case studies and a short benchmark with similar seq lengths.
[04:28] Speaker 1: uh-huh yeah
[04:30] Maya: small tangent — how bad are transcription/calls? (laughs)
[04:33] Daniel: (laughs) no worries.
[04:35] Daniel: security detail: for SSO we support SAML and all common IdPs; RBAC in Console; for KMS we integrate with major providers and you can wheel in an HSM if needed. encryption at rest and transit is standard.
[04:50] Priya: what about data retention? our legal team is sensitive to persisted logs.
[04:54] Alicia: we provide a retention policy and can limit logs; in Private deployments you control full retention. for Hosted there's options to disable storing customer prompts or to configure shorter retention windows.
[05:05] Arjun: can we run a short pilot, like 2 weeks, to validate latency and cost?
[05:09] Alicia: yes — quickstart pilot for 2 weeks works; we give credits, set up limits, and you run a small production-like workload. afterwards we review metrics and decide on next step (Dedicated or Private).
[05:19] Maya: what's the onboarding path for our devs — do you have SDK samples for node/python and an example repo?
[05:24] Daniel: yep we have SDKs, ready-made sample repos, and a sample frontend that demonstrates streaming, function-calling, and structured outputs. our quickstart repo includes automated scripts to spin up an example call and validate responses — that's what cuts TTFT down.
[05:40] Priya: network constraints — we have strict outbound egress rules, can we do a VPC peering?
[05:45] Daniel: for Private we support VPC peering and private endpoints; for Hosted we need specific egress rules; can you share exact CIDR/IP restrictions?
[05:53] Priya: yes I'll capture those and send to Daniel.
[05:57] Arjun: another technical question — how do you handle KV cache in multi-tenant Hosted mode? any risk of bleed?
[06:03] Daniel: KV is isolated per tenant. in Hosted we operate strong tenant isolation; Dedicated provides physical pool isolation which is typically preferred for high QPS workloads.
[06:12] Maya: curious about quantized model quality — do you see regressions?
[06:16] Daniel: quantization can slightly affect output in corner cases; we use quality monitoring and regressions alerts tied to eval prompt sets so you can catch QoR drops. for customer-facing summarization we usually suggest running eval sets with the quantized variant to validate.
[06:32] Alicia: quick note on rollouts — Redwood supports canary and A/B routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants if a new model underperforms. this is helpful during incremental upgrades.
[06:44] Maya: great. what's the typical decision timeline for teams like ours?
[06:48] Alicia: many teams run a 2-4 week pilot, then decide within a month whether to continue on Hosted, convert to Dedicated, or move to Private. for enterprise deals there's procurement time — 4-8 weeks usually.
[07:00] Arjun: procurement question: do you do standard enterprise contracts?
[07:03] Alicia: yes, we have enterprise agreements and can include SLAs for Dedicated.
[07:08] Speaker 2: (mumbled)
[07:10] Priya: ok can you outline what we'll get in the trial? specifics would help for our stakeholders.
[07:15] Alicia: trial specifics: $5k compute credits, sample models preloaded in the account, access to Console for logs/metrics, a sandbox rate limit increase on request, and a 30-min setup call with Daniel to wire up your sample calls.
[07:31] Maya: will the sandbox have telemetry so our PM can see token breakdowns?
[07:35] Daniel: yes token-level breakdowns, per-route latency, and cost analytics will be in Console.
[07:41] Arjun: if pilot goes well we'd likely want Dedicated reserved for predictable traffic and cost. what's minimum commit?
[07:48] Alicia: Dedicated minimums vary by region and GPU type; we can share a pricing sheet — many customers start with 1-2 reserved nodes for initial months.
[07:57] Maya: any gotchas? we want to avoid surprise egress bandwidth or storage fees.
[08:02] Daniel: transparent billing is core — Console exposes token vs infra cost split. we'll call out egress/storage specifically in the quote.
[08:11] Priya: we need an internal checklist for security signoff — SAML, SOC 2, audit logs, KMS, and support windows. can you provide a one-pager?
[08:19] Alicia: yes we'll send a security one-pager and SOC 2 report.
[08:23] Maya: on the demo side, can Daniel run an example of a quickstart live?
[08:27] Daniel: sure, if you want we can do a short demo now — or we can schedule a 30-min tech deep dive next week.
[08:34] Arjun: let's schedule the deep dive next week. today we're mostly collecting fit info.
[08:39] Alicia: ok next steps: I'll email the quickstart steps and credits detail, Daniel will send the benchmark checklist and sample curl commands, Priya will send network constraints. can we tentatively schedule the deep dive on 2028-07-11?
[08:52] Priya: works for me.
[08:54] Maya: works.
[08:55] Arjun: yes.
[08:56] Alicia: perfect. anything else before we wrap?
[08:58] Maya: one last Q — do you support private model uploads for compliance? e.g., we want to run our in-house model in Private.
[09:04] Daniel: yes Private/on-prem supports customer model hosting; we help with packaging and kernel selection but on-prem gives you more control.
[09:12] Priya: thanks all.
[09:14] Alicia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite. bye.

Call end.
